function_extent.symbol_extent_note: Linear disassembly of 0x007c6100-0x007c61bf shows 0x007c61b7 onward is INT3 padding, so 0x007c61a0-0x007c61b6 is a complete 23-byte function. The Ghidra decompiler's body is reported as if it had a second parameter (cViewer* pViewer) and an in_ECX alias, but no stack slot is read and the single return path is the RET at 0x007c61b3; the cViewer* parameter is a decompiler artifact, not an observed argument.

observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: EAX is the sole return register and both paths leave a 32-bit pointer in it: 0x007c61b0 MOV EAX,dword ptr [ECX + EAX*0x4] returns the raw handle read out of the mpCameras element, and 0x007c61b4 XOR EAX,EAX returns the null pointer. The staging type OpaqueCamera* models the SDK's App::ICamera* return of ICameraManager::GetActiveCamera; the imported SDK label SetViewer declares void, which the machine body contradicts. The bare pointer type is what the reconstructed source span declares, so it is stated here as modelled.

gpr_in.EAX: index, loaded from [ECX+0xa8] then reused as the scale/index
gpr_in.ECX: receiver, reloaded with [ECX+0x80] before the indexed load

gpr_out.EAX: returned pointer (element payload, or 0 on the negative-index path)

observed_mechanics: 0x007c61a0 MOV EAX,dword ptr [ECX + 0xa8] - load the 32-bit active index from receiver offset +0xa8 (SDK field mnActiveIndex).
0x007c61a6 TEST EAX,EAX / 0x007c61a8 JL 0x007c61b4 - the only branch; a signed negative index takes the null-return path.
0x007c61aa MOV ECX,dword ptr [ECX + 0x80] - load the contiguous element base from receiver offset +0x80 (SDK field mpCameras, the first word of the eastl::vector<ICameraPtr> header, i.e. mFirst).
0x007c61b0 MOV EAX,dword ptr [ECX + EAX*0x4] - scale-4 indexed load, so the vector element stride is 4 bytes and the loaded dword is the raw payload of one refcounted camera handle.
0x007c61b4 XOR EAX,EAX / 0x007c61b6 RET - null return for a negative active index.

No upper-bound compare against [ECX+0x84] (the vector mLast word) exists in this body, unlike the sibling routine at 0x007c61d0; a positive out-of-range active index reads past the element range without a guard.
No call instruction appears in the body: the routine is pure load, test, branch and indexed load, consistent with the briefing's no_open_internal_callees frontier reason.

control_flow: return element[active_index] from the contiguous base at +0x80;

naming_contradiction.assessment: The observed body is a getter, not a setter: it takes no stack argument, writes no receiver field, and returns a pointer. The one unambiguous writer of the SDK's mpViewer field at +0xB0 is the 7-instruction body at 0x007c6100 (MOV EAX,dword ptr [ESP+4]; MOV dword ptr [ECX+0xb0],EAX; RET 4). The prior committed analysis knowledgegraph/research/state-machines/empire-space.json already records the same reading at CONFIRMED level.
slot_order_evidence: The public SDK header Spore ModAPI/Spore/App/cCameraManager.h lists the virtual methods in declaration order, and cCameraManager is the only App::cCameraManager writer of +0xB0 observed at 0x007c6100, which occupies slot 7 of 0x014106a4 while the header's declaration index 5 is SetViewer - an offset of +2.
Slot 13 (0x007c6110) is the only other body that hashes a caller-supplied key and then dispatches virtually, matching declaration index 11 SetActiveCameraByKey - again +2.
Slot 18 (0x007c64e0) walks the +0x94 string16 vector with a 0x10-byte stride and then calls slot 0x50 virtually, matching declaration index 16 GetCameraID - again +2.
Slot 19 (0x007c61c0) is exactly (dword [ECX+0x84] - dword [ECX+0x80]) >> 2, the element count of the +0x80 vector, matching declaration index 17 GetCamerasCount - again +2.
Slot 20 (0x007c61d0) range-checks its stack argument against dword [ECX+0x84] minus dword [ECX+0x80] before indexing, matching declaration index 18 GetCameraAt - again +2.
naming_contradiction.slot_order_conclusion: Under a constant vtable_slot = declaration_index + 2 offset, slot 15 resolves to declaration index 13, which is GetActiveCamera. The offset is corroborated by five independent slot bodies but is an inference from the header declaration order, not a symbol recovered from the binary, so the rename is recorded and NOT applied.
secondary_sdk_address_defects_observed: SDK address 0x007c61b0 (declared SetActiveCameraByKey) falls inside this function's 23-byte body; the real keyed lookup is slot 13 at 0x007c6110.
SDK address 0x007c61f0 (declared GetActiveCameraID) is reported as interior to this function's containing region but is not a Ghidra function entry.

SDK address 0x007c6240 (declared GetActiveCamera) is interior to the larger body FUN_007c6200, which re-derives the same mpCameras[mnActiveIndex] expression at (*(int *)(param_1 + 0x80) + *(int *)(param_1 + 0xa8) * 4) - an independent witness of the expression recovered here.

semantic_findings: The 23-byte body at 0x007c61a0 reads the signed 32-bit field at +0xa8 and returns the 4-byte element payload from the contiguous base at +0x80 scaled by that field, returning the null pointer for a negative field value.

The +0x80 base is the first word of a 20-byte eastl vector header whose element stride is 4 bytes, matching SDK field mpCameras : eastl::vector<eastl::intrusive_ptr<App::ICamera>>; the 4-byte stride and the +0x84 / +0x88 words observed in the sibling count and indexer bodies are consistent with mFirst, mLast, mCapacity.
The routine has exactly one xref, a DATA entry in the 0x014106a4 vtable at index 15, and no direct call sites, so it is a virtual entry point reached only by dispatch.
The imported SDK name SetViewer does not match the machine body; the actual SetViewer semantics (store a cViewer* into +0xB0) are observed at 0x007c6100.
unresolved_questions: Is vtable slot 15 of 0x014106a4 definitely ICameraManager::GetActiveCamera? The declaration-order + 2 offset is corroborated by five independent slot bodies but is derived from the public SDK header's declaration order, not from a symbol in the binary, so the rename is not promoted here.

Why does the committed SDK address table place SetViewer at 0x007c61a0 and SetActiveCameraByKey at 0x007c61b0, both of which disagree with the machine? The defect is recorded, not repaired; repairing it would touch symbols owned by other queue rows.

The upper byte of the element payload is never inspected, so the recovered expression cannot distinguish a raw App::ICamera* from any other 4-byte handle; the App::ICamera* reading rests on the SDK vector element type.
No runtime or differential trace confirms the negative-index null return under real mnActiveIndex values, so the guard is machine-verified but not behaviourally validated.
The two slots preceding HandleMessage in the 0x014106a4 table (0x007c75d0, 0x007c76e0) are unidentified, so the table's inheritance depth and its two leading slots are not explained by this record.
